relations.subject: sgw:role
relations.evidence: A Sync Gateway role is a way of logically grouping users. Like the channel, a role is granted access to zero, one or more channels.

relations.subject: sgw:sync-function
relations.evidence: By default, every document in the collection is automatically assigned to a channel with the same name as the collection. This system automatically creates a channel with the collection's name.

relations.subject: sgw:channel-access-revocation
relations.evidence:
3.0 Breaking Change

Whenever a user loses access to a channel (or channels) all document in the channel(s) are auto-purged from local Couchbase Lite databases.
In Sync Gateway 2.x these documents remain in the local database on channel access loss.

cross_product_finding: This page is a shorter, near-identical subset of access-control-concepts.md (same Concept/Model/Context/Revocation sections, same quotes) - flagging for the coordinator as a likely duplicate-content pair, similar to the sync-function.json / sync-function-api-require-role-cmd.json split already noted in this tree. The one substantively new sentence here versus the concepts page is the explicit statement that 'access grants neither confer, nor constrain, the type of access' - i.e. a channel grant is undifferentiated with respect to read/write/delete. This is the clearest textual confirmation in the whole batch that SGW's channel model is fundamentally single-dimensional (you either can or can't reach a document via some channel) where server/'s privilege model is inherently multi-dimensional (separate named privileges per verb, e.g. query_select vs query_insert). Any write/delete-level distinction in SGW is bolted on afterward, entirely inside hand-written Sync Function code, not declared anywhere in the channel/role/user grant model itself.
